purpose: Probe the scroll-offset leg of hro_pol_live_board, which the scripted golden harness (workspace.cjs lines 382-399) does not exercise.
method: Local Chrome headless (--headless=new, --window-size=1280,720, innerHeight 625) loading the frozen solution/app/public/index.html, styles.css, js/board.js, js/threads.js, js/app.js copied byte-for-byte to the session scratchpad, with fetch/EventSource stubbed in-page to return a bootstrap of one job holding 12 Applied cards. Steps: scroll the window, open card 7's details, focus the note box and set 'Call back on Fri', record scrollY; mutate the stubbed bootstrap so one other card moves Applied->Screen; fire the stubbed 'changed' event (the app's real liveUpdate/refresh/render path); read again after 2 s. No server, no Docker, no SQLite. This is a client-only stub probe, not a judge run, Oracle grade or real-server observation.
reading: In all four variants (moved card above/below the viewport; window scrolled to 900 or to the bottom before opening details) window.scrollY is unchanged, the details stay open, the note text is unchanged and still document.activeElement. Page height drops 151 px but no clamp occurs because opening details focuses the sticky panel title, which pulls the bottom-scrolled page up to 1381 first. No scroll-anchoring adjustment was observed.
